activity_context.topic_title: Representing 2x2 Systems of Equations Using a Matrix Product

feedback.problem:
Represent the following system of equations using matrices:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x=y-1 \\ x=-y+1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we organize the system so that it’s in the correct order and  both $x$ and $y$ appear in each equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}x-y=-1 \\ x+y=1\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can write the system in the form $Ax=b,$ where

$$
A=[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the coefficient matrix,

$$
b=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of constants, and

$$
x=[\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]
$$

is the column vector of variables.

So, the equation $Ax=b$ becomes

$$
[\begin{aligned}1 & -1 \\ 1 & 1\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}x \\ y\end{aligned}]=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 1\end{aligned}].
$$
